purpose: The headless Topics computation-cost matrix under lazy materialization on and off, in runs labeled by mode, for docs/plans/topics-computation-cost.md.
head: fd9fa9a44b1d04c53cea863e5c46c48692d0da57

machine.caveat: The two matrix arms ran on a shared machine carrying load averages of roughly 20 to 40 against 10 logical CPUs, with unrelated Deno, Python and Xcode processes competing, and two toolsheds and a `cf piece new` were started during the off arm. Their elapsed times are two single samples under contention and are not a latency baseline. The repeat subset ran later at load averages of 2.7 to 6.7.

repeatSubset.purpose: Five rounds per arm over the all-backlinks cases at 4, 32 and 128 topics, for a timing distribution. The three 512-topic all-backlinks cases are left out: they are 1090 of the matrix's 2799 seconds and show no shape this span does not.

summary.determinism: Every case of the repeat subset produced one distinct set of counters across its five rounds in each arm, and that set equals the matrix arm's counters for the same case.

limitations: The matrix arms' elapsed times are single samples taken on a loaded shared machine and support no latency conclusion. The repeat subset is where the timing claims come from.

The repeat subset ran at a later head than the matrix arms (2303bcc1511c84af9228031091bcb3c4dc0503cc against fd9fa9a44b1d04c53cea863e5c46c48692d0da57); the commit between them touched browser benchmark files and documentation only, and the subset's counters equal the matrix arms', which is the evidence that the difference is inert for this measurement.

Server execution is not measured here. The headless fixture builds its runtime over an emulated storage manager with no memory server, so the serving loop has nothing to construct over; both modes hold serverExecution off.
The all-backlinks workload is a scaling probe rather than normal UI behavior, as the plan says. The per-workload split is what separates its cost from the topic-open workload's.
One trial of one case is not a rate. Every figure here comes from the runs in this file.
